rationale:
Split into four independent children. The supplied proof (steps 0–7) bundles four mathematical obligations of different kinds. Each is self-contained and now lives in its own child.

Children:
- planar_piece_measure (steps 0 and 2–4) is the GMT core: local constancy, in measure form, for an ambient integer multiplicity cycle on any open V with V ∩ Q connected and spt C ∩ V ⊆ Q. It restricts C to V, then shows the restriction is integer multiplicity, is a cycle, and has spt = spt C ∩ V. It then takes an orthonormal frame of Q, applies idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul, uses M_W(C) = M_W(C_V) = μ(W), and extends the result from open to Borel sets. It is stated for general n ≥ 1, V and Q, so it is reusable.
- plane_domain (step 1) is the topology: an open V_i containing P_i ∖ {0}, missing every other P_j, with V_i ∩ P_i connected (a punctured 2-plane, or the whole plane when q = 1).
- measure_sum_planes (step 0, step 5 and the additivity part of step 6) is the measure theory: μ({0}) = 0; μ vanishes off ⋃ P_i because spt C = supp μ; and finite additivity over the disjoint punctured planes.
- density_of_ball_mass (step 7) is generic: exactly homogeneous ball masses give the density, for any U, n, x, θ.

The parent proof then reduces to a short assembly:
1. Take V_i from plane_domain, and derive spt C ∩ V_i ⊆ P_i.
2. Get c_i from planar_piece_measure with n = 2.
3. For ρ > 0, measure_sum_planes with A = B_ρ(0) gives μ(B_ρ(0)) = Σ_i c_i·H²(P_i ∩ B_ρ(0)), using H²({0}) = 0. The sibling idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure makes this Σ_i c_i·ω_2·ρ².
4. dimred_im_mass_measure gives M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = μ(B_ρ(0)).
5. density_of_ball_mass with m = Σ_i c_i finishes the proof.

The children share no dependencies (no sibling edges), and none restates the parent, an ancestor or another DAG node. In particular two_dim_cone_density assumes a minimizing cone; no child does.

subproblems.title: An ambient integer multiplicity cycle carried by a plane over a connected planar domain has constant multiplicity there
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n, let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C), and let R be an integer multiplicity representation of C in ℝ^P (R : IMRep ℝ^P n with R.Represents C), with mass measure μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult), Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim Q = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n) such that V ∩ Q is connected and spt C ∩ V ⊆ Q. Then there is c ∈ ℕ with μ(E) = c·Hⁿ(E ∩ Q) for every Borel set E ⊆ V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen V → BoundaryVanishes C → R.Represents C → Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → IsConnected (V ∩ (Q : Set (Euclid P))) → C.support ∩ V ⊆ (Q : Set (Euclid P)) → ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ V → R.measure E = (c : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[n] (E ∩ (Q : Set (Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 2, 3 and 4 of the parent proof, i.e. the book's constancy step (chapter-07.txt lines 505–510: "since Θ^n(S, ·) is constant on P_i ∖ {0} (by the Constancy 2.34 of Ch. 6)"), carried out for one plane Q and one open domain V. Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := R.measure; M_W := massOn; ι := testFormOnInclusion (V ⊆ ℝ^P), so ιω is ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) regarded as a test form of ℝ^P with the same underlying differential form (testFormOnInclusion_coe).
1. (Restriction.) Let C_V := C.restrictDomain (V ⊆ ℝ^P) ∈ 𝒟_n(V). By definition (restrictDomain_apply), C_V(ω) = C(ιω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V).
2. (Integer multiplicity.) C is integer multiplicity, with witness R. Since V is open, the accepted Submission.dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (U := ℝ^P, V, T := C) shows that C_V is integer multiplicity.
3. (C_V is a cycle.) Since n ≥ 1, write n = m + 1. Then BoundaryVanishes C means C.boundary = 0, and we must show C_V.boundary = 0. Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(V). By boundary_apply and restrictDomain_apply, ∂C_V(β) = C_V(dβ) = C(ι(dβ)). The test forms ι(dβ) and d(ιβ) := exteriorDerivativeTestOn ℝ^P m (ιβ) of 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) have the same underlying form, exteriorDerivative β, so they are equal (Subtype.ext). Hence ∂C_V(β) = C(d(ιβ)) = ∂C(ιβ) = 0. By extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), C_V.boundary = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes C_V.
4. (Support.) V is open, and C(ιω) = 1·C_V(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), with 1 ≠ 0. So the accepted Submission.rsd_cmr_support_eq_inter (U := ℝ^P, T := C, T₀ := C_V, c := 1) gives spt C_V = spt C ∩ V. By hypothesis, spt C_V ⊆ Q.
   Direct argument for the inclusion spt C_V ⊆ spt C ∩ V that is used (parent step 2(c)): let x ∈ V ∖ spt C. Then x lies in an open set W₀ with compact closure on which C vanishes. Choose ε > 0 with closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ V. The set W := W₀ ∩ B_ε(x) is open, contains x, and has compact closure contained in closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ V. C_V vanishes on W: if ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) has tsupport ω ⊆ W, then C_V(ω) = C(ιω) = 0, because tsupport(ιω) = tsupport ω ⊆ W₀. So x lies in the zero region of C_V, i.e. x ∉ spt C_V. Since also spt C_V ⊆ V, we get spt C_V ⊆ spt C ∩ V.
5. (Orthonormal frame.) Q is finite-dimensional with finrank Q = n. Let b be stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q, reindexed from Fin (finrank Q) to Fin n by finCongr (finrank Q = n), and put τ_k := b_k ∈ ℝ^P for k ∈ Fin n.
   The inclusion Q → ℝ^P is a linear isometry (Q.subtypeₗᵢ), so τ is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry).
   Moreover range τ = Q.subtype '' range b. Hence span(range τ) = map Q.subtype (span(range b)) (Submodule.span_image). This equals map Q.subtype ⊤, since b is a basis, and map Q.subtype ⊤ = Q (Submodule.map_subtype_top). So span(range τ) = Q.
6. (Constancy.) Apply Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul (the constancy theorem, Simon Ch. 6, 2.34; a prerequisite of the ancestor node two_dim_cone_density) with n, V, S := C_V and τ. Its hypotheses hold:
   - 1 ≤ n, and V is open;
   - τ is orthonormal (step 5);
   - C_V is integer multiplicity (step 2), and BoundaryVanishes C_V (step 3);
   - spt C_V ⊆ Q = span(range τ) (steps 4 and 5);
   - V ∩ span(range τ) = V ∩ Q is connected (hypothesis and step 5).
   It yields c' ∈ ℤ such that M_W(C_V) = |c'|·Hⁿ(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ V (c'.natAbs; only this second conclusion is used).
7. (Mass on open sets.) Let W ⊆ V be open.
   - M_W(C) = M_W(C_V), by the accepted Submission.dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn (U := ℝ^P, V, W, S := C, S' := C_V). Its agreement hypothesis C(ιω) = C_V(ω) holds by definition for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V).
   - M_W(C) = μ(W), by part (a) of the accepted Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure (U := ℝ^P, which is open; T := C; R).
   With step 6, μ(W) = |c'|·Hⁿ(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ V.
8. (μ is finite on compact sets.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact; K is closed, hence Borel. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict, μ(K) = ∫⁻_{K ∩ R.carrier} R.mult dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{R.carrier ∩ K} R.mult dHⁿ. This is ≠ ∞ by the field R.locallyIntegrable_mult (K compact, K ⊆ ℝ^P).
9. (Borel extension.) Let ν := |c'| • (Hⁿ⌞Q). Then ν(G) = |c'|·Hⁿ(G ∩ Q) for every Borel G (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.restrict_apply). By step 7, μ(G) = ν(G) for every open G ⊆ V, and by step 8, μ(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V. So the accepted Submission.cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets (O := V, μ, ν) gives μ(E) = ν(E) = |c'|·Hⁿ(E ∩ Q) for every Borel E ⊆ V.
   Direct argument (parent step 4): let ν₁ := μ⌞V and ν₂ := ν⌞V.
   - For every open O ⊆ ℝ^P, O ∩ V is open and contained in V, so ν₁(O) = μ(O ∩ V) = ν(O ∩ V) = ν₂(O) by step 7.
   - The balls B_k(0), k ∈ ℕ, increase to ℝ^P, and ν₁(B_k(0)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, k)) < ∞ by step 8.
   - Open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra.
   So ν₁ = ν₂ (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion), and for Borel E ⊆ V, μ(E) = ν₁(E) = ν₂(E) = ν(E).
10. Taking c := |c'| = c'.natAbs ∈ ℕ, we get μ(E) = c·Hⁿ(E ∩ Q) for every Borel E ⊆ V. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict C to V: C_V := C.restrictDomain is integer multiplicity (dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity) and a cycle, because ι(dβ) = d(ιβ) as test forms.
spt C_V = spt C ∩ V ⊆ Q (rsd_cmr_support_eq_inter with c = 1).
An orthonormal basis of Q, pushed into ℝ^P, is an orthonormal τ with span(range τ) = Q.
idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul gives c' ∈ ℤ with M_W(C_V) = |c'|·Hⁿ(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ V.
M_W(C) = M_W(C_V) = μ(W) for open W ⊆ V (dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn, dimred_im_mass_measure).
μ is finite on compact sets (locallyIntegrable_mult), so the open-set identity extends to every Borel E ⊆ V (cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets, or π–λ uniqueness); take c = |c'|.

subproblems.title: An open domain containing a punctured 2-plane, avoiding the other planes, whose trace on the plane is connected
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let P_1, …, P_q (a family Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ ℝ^P) be linear subspaces of ℝ^P, and let i ∈ Fin q be such that dim P_i = 2 and P_i ∩ P_j = {0} (Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) for every j ≠ i. Then there is an open set V ⊆ ℝ^P such that V ∩ P_i is connected, P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V, and V is disjoint from P_j for every j ≠ i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (i : Fin q), Module.finrank ℝ (Ps i) = 2 → (∀ j, j ≠ i → Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) → ∃ V : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen V ∧ IsConnected (V ∩ (Ps i : Set (Euclid P))) ∧ (Ps i : Set (Euclid P)) \ {0} ⊆ V ∧ ∀ j, j ≠ i → Disjoint V (Ps j : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the domains V_i := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j), parts (i) and (ii) and the disjointness used in part (iii).
1. (Definition and openness.) Let F := ⋃_{j ∈ Fin q, j ≠ i} P_j and V := ℝ^P ∖ F. Each P_j is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). The index set {j ∈ Fin q | j ≠ i} is finite, so F is closed as a finite union of closed sets (Set.Finite.isClosed_biUnion). Hence V is open.
2. (P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V.) Let x ∈ P_i with x ≠ 0, and suppose x ∈ F. Then x ∈ P_j for some j ≠ i, so x ∈ P_i ⊓ P_j (Submodule.mem_inf). By hypothesis P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥, so x = 0 (Submodule.mem_bot), a contradiction. Hence x ∈ V.
3. (V is disjoint from P_j for j ≠ i.) For j ≠ i, P_j ⊆ F = ℝ^P ∖ V.
4. (V ∩ P_i is connected.) We distinguish two cases.
   Case (a): no j ∈ Fin q with j ≠ i exists. Then F = ∅ and V = ℝ^P, so V ∩ P_i = P_i. This set is convex (Submodule.convex) and nonempty (0 ∈ P_i), hence connected (Convex.isConnected).
   Case (b): some j ≠ i exists. Then 0 ∈ P_j ⊆ F, so 0 ∉ V; together with step 2, V ∩ P_i = P_i ∖ {0}.
   - Regard P_i as a real normed space with the induced norm. Its rank equals finrank P_i = 2 > 1 (Module.finrank_eq_rank).
   - By Mathlib's isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank, the set {0}ᶜ ⊆ P_i is connected.
   - The inclusion Subtype.val : P_i → ℝ^P is continuous, and it maps {0}ᶜ exactly onto P_i ∖ {0}: an element of P_i is nonzero iff its image is nonzero (Subtype.ext).
   So P_i ∖ {0} = V ∩ P_i is connected (IsConnected.image).
   Elementary alternative for case (b), which avoids importing Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected: take an orthonormal basis e₁, e₂ of P_i. The map (r, t) ↦ r(cos t·e₁ + sin t·e₂) is continuous on (0, ∞) × ℝ, which is convex and hence connected. It maps this set onto P_i ∖ {0}:
   - every image point lies in P_i and has norm r > 0;
   - a nonzero x = a e₁ + b e₂ ∈ P_i has z := a + b·i ≠ 0 in ℂ, and x = |z|(cos(arg z)·e₁ + sin(arg z)·e₂) by Complex.cos_arg and Complex.sin_arg.
5. Steps 1–4 show that V is open, V ∩ P_i is connected, P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V, and V is disjoint from P_j for every j ≠ i. ∎
Implementation note: isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected, which the frozen contract does not import. Either add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected` to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean (accepted candidates have added Mathlib imports before) or use the elementary alternative in step 4(b).
proof_key_steps: Take V := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j; finite-dimensional subspaces are closed, so V is open.
P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V because P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥ for j ≠ i, and P_j ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ V for j ≠ i.
If no j ≠ i exists, V ∩ P_i = P_i is convex and nonempty, hence connected.
Otherwise 0 ∉ V, so V ∩ P_i = P_i ∖ {0}: the image of the connected set {0}ᶜ of the space P_i (rank 2 > 1, isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank) under the continuous inclusion.

subproblems.title: Exactly homogeneous ball masses determine the density
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, θ ∈ ℝ with θ ≥ 0, and r > 0. Suppose that M_{B_ρ(x)}(T) = ofReal(θ)·(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) in [0, ∞] for every ρ with 0 < ρ < r, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the volume of the unit ball of ℝⁿ. Then HasMassDensity T x θ, i.e. Θⁿ(μ_T, x) = θ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (θ r : ℝ), 0 ≤ θ → 0 < r → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r → T.massOn (ball x ρ) = ENNReal.ofReal θ * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) → HasMassDensity T x θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof.
1. (0 < ω_n < ∞.) ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0)), the volume of the open unit ball of Euclid n.
   - B_1(0) is open and nonempty (it contains 0), and volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpen.measure_pos). So ω_n ≠ 0.
   - Euclid n is a proper space and volume is finite on compact sets, so volume(B_1(0)) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). So ω_n ≠ ∞.
   (This also covers n = 0, where Euclid 0 is a point.)
2. (Nondegenerate normalization.) Let 0 < ρ < r and a_ρ := ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ). Since ρⁿ > 0 (pow_pos), ofReal(ρⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞) (ENNReal.ofReal_pos, ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top). With step 1, a_ρ ≠ 0 (mul_ne_zero) and a_ρ ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
3. (The ratio is constant.) For 0 < ρ < r, the hypothesis and step 2 give M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/a_ρ = (ofReal(θ)·a_ρ)/a_ρ = ofReal(θ) (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right).
4. (Limit.) Since r > 0, the interval (0, r) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). By step 3, the function ρ ↦ M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) is eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0 to the constant ofReal(θ). Hence it tends to ofReal(θ) (tendsto_const_nhds.congr').
5. Together with the hypothesis 0 ≤ θ, this is exactly the definition of HasMassDensity T x θ. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n is the volume of a nonempty bounded open set, so 0 < ω_n < ∞; hence 0 < ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ) < ∞ for ρ > 0.
For 0 < ρ < r the density ratio equals ofReal(θ)·a/a = ofReal(θ).
(0, r) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, so the ratio is eventually constant and tends to ofReal(θ); with θ ≥ 0 this is HasMassDensity T x θ.

subproblems.title: The mass measure of a current carried by planes through 0 splits over the punctured planes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, q ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n, let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), let R be an integer multiplicity representation of C in ℝ^P (R.Represents C) with mass measure μ := R.measure, and let P_1, …, P_q (Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ ℝ^P) be linear subspaces of ℝ^P with P_i ∩ P_j = {0} (Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) for i ≠ j, such that every x ∈ spt C with x ≠ 0 lies in some P_i. Then μ(A) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin q} μ(A ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n q : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → R.Represents C → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) → (∀ x ∈ C.support, x ≠ 0 → ∃ i, x ∈ Ps i) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ i, R.measure (A ∩ ((Ps i : Set (Euclid P)) \ {0}))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 5 of the parent proof and the finite-additivity part of its step 6. Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult).
1. (Hⁿ({0}) = 0.) Since 0 < n, Mathlib's euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (d₁ := 0 < d₂ := n, s := {0}) gives μHE[n]({0}) = 0 or μHE[0]({0}) = ∞. The second alternative is impossible: μHE[0] = μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]({0}) = 1 ≠ ∞ (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence Hⁿ({0}) = 0.
2. (μ({0}) = 0.) {0} is closed, hence Borel, so μ({0}) = ∫⁻_{{0}} R.mult d(Hⁿ⌞R.carrier) by withDensity_apply. Also (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier)({0}) ≤ Hⁿ({0}) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply_le), so the integral vanishes (setLIntegral_measure_zero).
3. (spt C is the support of μ.) The accepted Submission.imrep_represents_support_eq_inter_measure_support (U := ℝ^P, open; T := C; R) gives spt C = ℝ^P ∩ μ.support = μ.support. Here μ.support is the support of the measure μ: the points all of whose neighbourhoods have positive μ-measure.
4. (Null set off the planes.) Let O := ℝ^P ∖ ({0} ∪ ⋃_{i ∈ Fin q} P_i). Then O ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ μ.support: if x ∈ O ∩ μ.support, then x ∈ spt C by step 3 and x ≠ 0, so the hypothesis puts x in some P_i, contradicting x ∈ O. Since ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, μ(ℝ^P ∖ μ.support) = 0 (Measure.measure_compl_support). So μ(O) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
   Alternative (parent step 5): O is open (each P_i is closed) and disjoint from spt C. By part (b) of the accepted Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure, every x ∈ O has ε_x > 0 with μ(B_{ε_x}(x)) = 0. Since ℝ^P is second countable, countably many of these balls cover O (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable), so μ(O) = 0.
5. (The pieces.) Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, and set A_i := A ∩ (P_i ∖ {0}) for i ∈ Fin q.
   - Each A_i is Borel, since P_i is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and {0} is closed.
   - The A_i are pairwise disjoint: if x ∈ A_i ∩ A_j with i ≠ j, then x ∈ P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥ (Submodule.mem_inf, hypothesis, Submodule.mem_bot), so x = 0, contradicting x ∉ {0}.
   By countable additivity over the finite index type Fin q, μ(⋃_i A_i) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin q} μ(A_i) (measure_iUnion, tsum_fintype).
6. (The remainder is null.) A ∖ ⋃_i A_i ⊆ {0} ∪ O: if x ∈ A, x ∉ ⋃_i A_i and x ≠ 0, then x ∉ P_i for every i (otherwise x ∈ A_i), so x ∈ O. By steps 2 and 4, μ(A ∖ ⋃_i A_i) ≤ μ({0} ∪ O) = 0 (measure_union_null, measure_mono_null).
7. (Conclusion.) Since ⋃_i A_i ⊆ A and μ(A ∖ ⋃_i A_i) = 0, μ(A) = μ(⋃_i A_i) (measure_eq_measure_of_null_sdiff). By step 5 this equals Σ_{i ∈ Fin q} μ(A ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})). For q = 0 the sum is 0, and the argument shows μ(A) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ({0}) = 0 for n ≥ 1, and μ ≪ Hⁿ, so μ({0}) = 0.
spt C = supp μ (imrep_represents_support_eq_inter_measure_support), so the set O off {0} ∪ ⋃ P_i misses supp μ and μ(O) = 0 (measure_compl_support).
The sets A ∩ (P_i ∖ {0}) are Borel and pairwise disjoint (P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥), so finite additivity applies.
A minus their union lies in {0} ∪ O, which is μ-null, so μ(A) = Σ_i μ(A ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})).
